title: Address late-ingest and rate-limit artifacts in per-model funnel metrics
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
Per-model funnel charts and stacked usage heatmaps in Console are showing transient negative dips and double-count spikes after late/backfilled ingest. This appears correlated with (a) synthetic 'throttled' events emitted by the rate-limiter when requests are proxied between shards during maintenance windows, and (b) a mismatch between our aggregation pipeline which currently aligns by ingestion_time and the rest of the system which aligns by event_time.

Customer impact:
- Medium/High: customers see inconsistent daily per-model token counts, leading to billing confusion and SRE escalations for quota enforcement anomalies. Some tenants reported alerts for quota breaches that were later reversed.

What we've reproduced so far:
- Replayed a delayed shard segment (simulating a late backfill) and observed negative deltas in the hourly diffs of the funnel charts for models that had both streaming and batch traffic.
- Isolated events with a 'synthetic=true' rate_limiter flag (introduced last year to mark replay-proxies) that were previously counted as regular usage in aggregate rollups.
- Confirmed by sampling raw events that ingestion_time != event_time for ~2.4% of affected rows; our hourly windowing uses ingestion_time which causes late rows to be folded into previous buckets and sometimes cancel out earlier aggregated counts when dedup logic runs.

Root causes (hypothesis -> evidence):
1) Synthetic rate-limiter events are not excluded from billing aggregation. Evidence: query on raw_events showed token_count>0 and synthetic=true across shards during maintenance windows.
2) Aggregation watermark uses ingestion_time causing retroactive adjustments when late rows arrive or are reprocessed. Evidence: backfill run logs and window watermark demonstrates event_time attribute is ignored for sharded merges.
3) Dedup / merge logic occasionally uses a last-write-wins policy keyed on shard_offset which can lead to negative correction when a previously-shadowed row is replaced. Evidence: merge traces in kinesis consumer logs.

Proposed fix (multi-part):
A) Ingestion filter: update the streaming pipeline (ingest-consumer) to mark or drop synthetic rate-limiter events for billing aggregates (configurable by tenant). Default behavior: drop synthetic events from billing rollups.
B) Windowing alignment: change aggregate job (metrics-aggregator) to use event_time as primary time alignment and use ingestion_time only as a fallback. Add a bounded-lateness policy of 48 hours for accepting late events into the event_time buckets.
C) Merge/dedup stabilization: change dedup to prefer earliest-seen canonical_id for usage attribution rather than last-write-wins, and emit a tombstone record when rewriting a previously-counted row to avoid negative corrections.
D) Backfill rewriter: a controlled reprocessor job that rewrites historical late/backfilled rows to set synthetic=false/true appropriately and re-emits corrected aggregate deltas for affected hourly buckets.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary, 2 days): Deploy ingestion filter + event_time alignment to a small set of low-traffic tenants and monitor per-tenant delta metrics.
- Phase 2 (48h monitoring): Run backfill rewriter for the canary group; validate Console charts and billing ledgers are stable.
- Phase 3 (ramp): Expand to 25% of tenants, then 75% after checks.
- Phase 4 (all): Full rollout and schedule a final run of full-historical correction for last 30 days.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for ingestion filter and dedup logic (edge cases for identical shard_offsets).
- Integration test replay harness: replay synthetic and late rows into a test cluster and assert no negative diffs and that per-model totals are monotonic within the bounded-lateness window.
- Load test: ensure new event_time windowing maintains latency SLO of aggregator job (<5s per event under steady load).

Monitoring / Alerts to add:
- New dashboard: "Late-ingest correction rate" (percent of hourly buckets adjusted by rewriter per tenant).
- Alert: >0.1% of buckets with negative corrections in 1h window for production tenants -> page on-call.
- Canary checks: compare ledger totals vs Console totals after rewriter runs.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Rewriting historical buckets could cause confusion on billing history. Mitigation: communicate to billing ops and prefix all ledger adjustments with admin tags and send tenant notifications for adjustments >$5.
- Risk: Event_time alignment may accept maliciously old events. Mitigation: enforce bounded-lateness (48h) and drop events older than 7 days with audit trace.

Artifacts & references:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Backfill+Late+Ingest+Design
- Reproducer script (internal): gs://redwood-internal/repro/late_ingest_replay_2026-02-26.sh
- Sample query used to identify synthetic rows:
  SELECT model_id, count(*), sum(token_count), synthetic FROM raw_events WHERE ingestion_time BETWEEN '2026-02-15' AND '2026-02-16' GROUP BY model_id, synthetic ORDER BY sum(token_count) DESC LIMIT 50;
- Proposed PR (ingestion filter): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345

Acceptance criteria:
- No negative deltas in per-model hourly funnel charts for canary tenants for 72h after deployment.
- Aggregate billing ledger discrepancies reduced to <0.01% after backfill rewriter run.
- No dropped usage for tenants that do not opt-in to synthetic-event-drop (configurable).

Next steps:
- Spike (#1): implement ingestion filter patch and verify behavioral change locally. Owner: Liam. Due: 2026-03-05.
- Spike (#2): implement event_time alignment in aggregator, add unit tests. Owner: Maya. Due: 2026-03-08.
- Coordination: schedule run with billing-ops for communication window. Owner: Priya Rao. Due: 2026-03-09.
